title: Do the two answers match?
starter:
import math
import struct


def same_f32(want: list[float], got: list[float]) -> bool:
    return False
hints: Check the lengths first. Then walk the pairs with `zip(want, got)` and return `False` at the first pair that does not match.
`a == b` is wrong twice: it says `0.0` equals `-0.0`, and it says a NaN does not equal a NaN. Handle NaN first with `math.isnan(a) and math.isnan(b)`.
For everything else compare the bits: `struct.pack("<f", a) == struct.pack("<f", b)` is true only when all 32 bits agree.
prompt: Write same_f32(want, got). Both are lists of floats that hold f32 values: want from the interpreter, got read back from the C program. Return True when the lists have the same length and every pair has the same 32 bits. One exception: a NaN matches any NaN. So 0.0 and -0.0 do not match, even though 0.0 == -0.0 is True in Python.

answer.explain: Comparing with `==` asks whether two floats have the same value, which treats `0.0` and `-0.0` as equal and a NaN as unequal to everything. Packing each value into its 4 bytes compares the bits instead, and a separate `math.isnan` check lets any NaN match any NaN, which is the rule the grader uses for buffers.
